skill.author: srinitude

security_audit.summary: All 59 static findings are false positives caused by documentation syntax, local validation text, restricted configuration access, or a controlled test subprocess. A semantic review found one medium concern: the skill intentionally runs a bundled Python script before every direct reply, even when time is irrelevant.

remediation.issue: The default trigger executes a local script for every direct user message.
remediation.suggestion: Default to temporal requests and provide an explicit opt-in for every-turn mode. Keep the command fixed to the verified bundled script.

semantic_findings.title: Unconditional Per-Turn Script Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill requires running its bundled Python clock script before every direct user reply, including requests unrelated to time. The command is fixed and local, but the broad trigger increases automatic code-execution exposure.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: SKILL.md explicitly requires execution before every direct reply and directs the host to run the bundled script once. The fixed script path limits command-injection risk.

content.user_title: Refresh Every Reply With Current Date and Time
content.value_statement: Long conversations can rely on stale dates, times, or timezone assumptions. This skill acquires a fresh local clock anchor and resolves temporal language before replying.
actual_capabilities: Runs a bundled Python script to acquire one fresh clock anchor.
Uses an explicit IANA timezone, PROFILE_TIMEZONE, or system-local time.
Returns date, time, weekday, timezone, abbreviation, and UTC offset.
Resolves relative temporal language before date-sensitive actions.
Adds visible date-time prefixes to normal user-facing replies.
Fails closed when the clock command or timezone configuration is invalid.
limitations: Requires a working Python interpreter with zoneinfo support.
Cannot infer the intended timezone from conversational text.
Does not create reminders, calendar events, deployments, or scheduled jobs.
Adds execution overhead and a visible prefix to every direct reply.

use_cases.title: Clarify Relative Deadlines
use_cases.description: Resolve terms such as tomorrow or next Friday against a fresh timezone-aware anchor.

use_cases.title: Prepare Absolute Tool Arguments
use_cases.description: Convert relative dates into explicit values before calendar, search, or deployment tools run.

use_cases.title: Track Time Across Long Sessions
use_cases.description: Refresh temporal context after new messages, resumes, compaction, or local date changes.

prompt_templates.title: Check Current Time
prompt_templates.prompt: What is the current date and time in my configured timezone?
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a fresh clock reading

prompt_templates.title: Resolve a Relative Date
prompt_templates.prompt: Using the fresh clock anchor, tell me the exact date for tomorrow and preserve my original wording.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify an Ambiguous Weekday
prompt_templates.prompt: I need this next Friday. Show the possible absolute dates and ask one concise question if the phrase is ambiguous.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Time-Bounded Actions
prompt_templates.prompt: Resolve every relative date in this request before any tool call. Use absolute timestamps with timezone offsets and identify unresolved assumptions.

output_examples.input: Schedule the review for next Friday.
output_examples.output: [2026-08-31 15:48:20 UTC] Does next Friday mean September 4 or September 11, 2026?

output_examples.input: Use the configured timezone for this deadline.
output_examples.output: [2026-08-31 15:48:20 UTC] The deadline will use UTC unless you provide another valid IANA timezone.

best_practices: Provide an explicit IANA timezone when system-local time is not appropriate.
Acquire the anchor before interpreting relative dates or calling date-sensitive tools.
Ask one concise question when a weekday phrase has multiple common meanings.
anti_patterns: Do not reuse an anchor captured before the newest direct user message.
Do not guess a date after invalid timezone input or clock failure.
Do not treat this skill as a reminder, calendar, or scheduling service.

faq.question: Which timezone does the skill use?
faq.answer: An explicit IANA timezone wins, followed by PROFILE_TIMEZONE, then the system-local timezone.

faq.question: Does it run on every message?
faq.answer: Yes. The current contract runs once before every direct user reply, including messages without temporal language.

faq.question: Can it infer my timezone from conversation?
faq.answer: No. Supply a valid IANA timezone through the supported argument or environment configuration.

faq.question: What happens when the timezone is invalid?
faq.answer: The script exits with an error, emits no success result, and blocks date-dependent work.

faq.question: Can it create reminders or calendar events?
faq.answer: No. It prepares absolute date-time values, while another capability must perform those actions.

faq.question: Why does each reply include a timestamp?
faq.answer: The visible prefix records which fresh clock anchor governed that reply and helps identify stale temporal context.
